prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1117; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a side impact at an intersection and stated the other vehicle entered from the right against a red signal. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been cooperative with requests for information.

Entry 2: Responding officer's report and two independent witnesses place the claimant's vehicle at the intersection at the time of the collision. The other driver's account matches the claimant's description of how the crash occurred.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene show damage to the driver's side that is largely consistent with the described impact. A few older scratches appear in the same area, and further inspection will determine whether they predate this loss.

Entry 4: Claimant reports neck and back strain, which is a plausible injury for a collision of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the information gathered so far.

Entry 5: Claimant provided a follow-up statement adding a few small details, such as the approximate position of the other vehicle. The core account has not changed from the initial report. Treatment records show a typical course of care that has tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Policy records confirm the driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before coverage began. The claim remains open pending completion of the vehicle inspection.
